Consult Summary:
- 26-year-old with 3-hour history of chest tightness, wheeze, and shortness of breath following a recent cold; associated cough, sore throat, and runny nose. Known asthma with past severe exacerbation; currently out of inhalers.
- Plan includes restarting inhaled therapy (Ventolin and Clenil Modulite), a short course of oral steroids, spacer prescription, and rest/work leave; patient advised to seek care if symptoms worsen or if frequent albuterol use is required.

Problem List:

Issue 1:
- Acute asthma exacerbation likely triggered by recent viral URI.
- Timeline: symptoms started ~3 hours ago; persistent cough (non-productive), wheeze, chest tightness, mild exertional dyspnea; nocturnal symptoms suggested but not prominent.
- Associated symptoms: runny nose, sore throat; feeling under the weather earlier.
- Symptoms management history: previously has asthma; not currently using inhalers (ran out ~1 week ago); no current fever or chest pain.
- Social/medication considerations: no current inhaler use; family history of asthma; personal history of eczema; dust allergy; milk protein allergy in childhood.
- Past evaluations/differential: prior severe asthma exacerbation requiring intubation in adolescence.

Issue 2:
- Chronic asthma with episodic exacerbations; risk factors for poor control (non-adherence to inhalers recently).
- Timeline: history from childhood to present; past hospital admission for asthma exacerbation with intubation (age ~16–17).
- Systems review: no current chest pain; exercise-induced breathlessness on stairs noted.
- Social/medication considerations: family history of asthma; history of eczema; dust allergy; not on maintenance therapy currently.
- Examination/diagnosis: no objective exam findings documented.

Issue 3:
- Acute management plan for asthma exacerbation.
- Interventions planned: initiate inhaled therapy (beclomethasone Clenil Modulite daily morning; Salbutamol Ventolin PRN); provide spacer; short course oral corticosteroids (two tablets each morning for 5 days; exact dose not documented); return precautions; rest with up to 7 days off work.
- Follow-up/monitoring: advised to seek medical attention if Ventolin needed more than every 3 hours or if symptoms worsen; plan to deliver prescriptions within the hour.
- Patient understanding: acknowledged plan and agreed to spacer use; expressed desire to avoid intubation.

Medications:
- Salbutamol (Ventolin) inhaler — PRN; dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Beclomethasone inhaler (Clenil Modulite) — morning use; dose not documented.
- Oral corticosteroids — two tablets in the morning for 5 days; exact dose not documented.
- Spacer device — prescribed to aid inhalation; no dose.

Allergies:
- Drug allergies: none reported.
- Other allergies: dust allergy; hay fever; milk protein allergy (childhood).

Past Medical History:
- Asthma (longstanding; prior severe exacerbation with intubation in adolescence).
- Hay fever/allergic rhinitis.
- Eczema (personal history; childhood).
- Milk protein allergy (childhood).

Social History:
- Not documented beyond recent university absence; no smoking or alcohol details provided.

Preventative History:
- Not documented.

Physical Examination:
- No vitals or objective examination findings recorded in transcript.

Plan:
- Start/renew inhaled maintenance and rescue therapy:
  - Clenil Modulite (beclomethasone) inhaler — morning use; dosage not documented.
  - Salbutamol (Ventolin) inhaler — PRN; dosage/frequency not documented.
  - Provide spacer device; instructions to use spacer with inhalers.
- Short course systemic corticosteroids:
  - Oral steroids for 5 days; two tablets in the morning (exact tablet strength not documented).
- Return/work considerations:
  - Self-certify 7 days off work; rest until improved.
  - Seek medical attention if shortness of breath worsens, chest pain occurs, or Ventolin use exceeds every 3 hours.
- Follow-up/education:
  - Plan to have inhalers delivered within an hour.
  - Emphasized importance of avoiding intubation; provided instructions on spacer use.

Document Quality:

- Missing elements:
  - Vitals (BP, HR, RR, SpO2, temperature) and explicit auscultation findings.
  - Spirometry/peak expiratory flow measurements.
  - Complete medication dosing specifics (tablet strength for steroids; inhaler dosages/frequencies beyond PRN or morning use).
  - Comprehensive social history (smoking status, alcohol, living situation) and preventive history (vaccinations, prior optometry/skin checks).
  - Immunization status and up-to-date preventative care not documented.

- Internal conflicts:
  - None evident in transcript.

- Transcript quality:
  - Generally clear; occasional brief interruptions but overall understandable. No critical inconsistencies detected.
